answer: History-weighted job lotteries stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each job is raffled, tickets equal to verified jobs completed. Second, fresh accounts hold almost no tickets, so a fleet of copies cannot crowd out honest agents. Third, the winner posts a $20 bond and the draw uses a public random function. Fourth, fraud burns tickets and bond, banning the agent a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 10,000 verified jobs plus $20,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is a knoll, not a delta of copies, its pulse steady work, like a market stall winning the weekly pitch draw by showing up.
